Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

nina: that envelope is mine, yes, it has the blue pharmacy logo on it. i’m not expecting anything else today. if you see a flat white mailer addressed to Nina Patel, leave it at the desk and i’ll pick it up tomorrow when i’m coming back from work.

nina: please don’t include my envelope in that message as a pickup request. i’d rather collect it tomorrow myself, and the desk already knows it’s mine from the label. the white mailer is thin and could slide behind the boxes, so look along the lower shelf too.

mara: okay, i’ve sent the desk message for the three boxes only. i used the resident app, and they replied with a thumbs-up, no other details. i’ll take a photo of the labels when we’re at the counter so we can make sure the parcels belong to our apartment.

eli: one small thing: the stairwell door on our floor is propped open for the painter, but he said he’ll be working there until 6:45. we can use the lift both ways if it’s running, and keep the trolley parked against the wall so it doesn’t block anyone coming through.

mara: i’ll bring the reusable bags too, though they’re probably only useful for the envelope or any loose packing paper. the boxes are bigger than the bags. the kitchen shelf carton is marked 12 kg on the side, so let’s each take one end rather than try to balance it on the trolley.

nina: the painter just moved his drop cloth away from the stairwell, so that route is clear now. i’m leaving the trolley outside my door until Eli picks it up; please don’t leave it in the lobby overnight because the cleaner stacks the recycling carts there at 7.

eli: got it. i’m heading over in five minutes, and i’ll check that the trolley strap is still tucked under the handle. it was loose last week. if the lift is occupied when we arrive, we can wait by the mailboxes rather than stand in front of the parcel room entrance.

mara: i’ll be downstairs at 6:15, wearing the yellow rain jacket. my phone’s battery is at 38%, so if the app drops out i can show the desk the message thread on the screen. the parcel room is on the left after the mailboxes, not through the laundry door.

nina: i found the little receipt from when the trolley was repaired; it’s in the basket by my keys if you need the wheel shop’s number later. no need to take it tonight, though. the spare umbrella beside it is mine, and it has a cracked handle, so please leave that one where it is.

eli: thanks, Nina. i’ll take the trolley and leave the receipt and umbrella there. also, the lobby mat is drying now, but there’s still a damp patch near the corner by the plant stand. i’ll steer around it so the boxes don’t pick up water on the bottom.

mara: one last practical detail, the building’s parcel room light switch is just inside the door on the right. it sometimes doesn’t come on automatically. i’ll have my phone flashlight ready, and once we’ve checked the labels we can take the three boxes straight to our apartment.", "output": "mara: Hey, can we sort out the parcel room pickup for our place before dinner?
